next_state_election.name: General Election
next_state_election.source_name: New York State Board of Elections

glance_notes.source_name: New York State Board of Elections — Registration and Voting Deadlines
glance_notes.text: 2026 General Election Registration Deadline: To vote in New York's November 3, 2026 General Election, a voter registration application must be received by the appropriate Board of Elections no later than October 24, 2026.

glance_notes.source_name: New York State Board of Elections — Early Voting
glance_notes.text: Early Voting October 24–November 1: New York provides nine days of in-person early voting before the General Election. For the November 3, 2026 General Election, early voting runs from October 24 through November 1. Hours vary by county.

glance_notes.source_name: New York State Board of Elections — Request a Ballot
glance_notes.text: Early Mail Voting Available to All Registered Voters: New York registered voters may request an early mail ballot without providing an excuse. Absentee ballots remain a separate option for voters who meet one of New York's qualifying absentee reasons.

register.label: Register to Vote
register.content: Eligible New York residents may register online, by mail, in person at a County Board of Elections, through the Department of Motor Vehicles or through participating state agency voter registration centers. To register, a person must be a U.S. citizen, be at least 18 years old by Election Day and meet New York's residency and voter-eligibility requirements. A person may preregister beginning at age 16, but cannot vote until eligible. A person convicted of a felony may register and vote after release from incarceration, including while on parole or probation, provided all other eligibility requirements are met.
register.glance_value: Online, mail, county office, DMV or participating agencies
register.source_name: New York State Board of Elections — Register to Vote
register.internal_note: The State Board directly provides online, mail and in-person registration resources and directs voters to DMV and agency-based registration. New York's current felony-voting rule restores voting rights upon release from incarceration. Older descriptions requiring completion of parole are outdated. New York also permits preregistration beginning at age 16.

check_registration.label: Check Voter Registration
check_registration.content: Use the New York State Board of Elections' official voter lookup to confirm your registration status and find your Election Day and early-voting polling locations. If your registration information is incorrect or missing, contact your County Board of Elections.
check_registration.glance_value: Check registration and voting locations online
check_registration.source_name: New York State Board of Elections — Voter Lookup
check_registration.internal_note: The State Board's Ways to Vote page directly identifies its poll-site and voter lookup as the official method to confirm registration status and find Election Day and early-voting polling places.

deadlines.label: Registration Deadlines
deadlines.content: For New York's November 3, 2026 General Election, voter registration applications submitted by mail or in person must be received by the appropriate Board of Elections no later than Saturday, October 24, 2026. New York does not provide general same-day voter registration during early voting or on Election Day.
deadlines.source_name: New York State Board of Elections — Registration and Voting Deadlines
deadlines.internal_note: The State Board's current 2026 deadline page directly states that both mail and in-person applications must be received by October 24 to qualify for the November 3 General Election. The official 2026 Political Calendar cites Election Law Sections 5-210, 5-211 and 5-212. Address changes received by October 19 must be processed for the General Election.

polling_place.label: Find a Polling Place
polling_place.content: Use New York's official voter lookup to find your Election Day polling site and early-voting location. Election Day voters generally vote at the polling place assigned to their residential address. Early-voting arrangements differ: outside New York City, voters may use any of the early-voting centers assigned to them within their county, while New York City voters are assigned to a specific early-voting site.
polling_place.glance_value: Use the official Poll Site and Voter Lookup
polling_place.source_name: New York State Board of Elections — Voter Lookup
polling_place.internal_note: The State Board directly distinguishes early-voting procedures inside and outside New York City. Outside NYC, voters may visit any of their assigned early-voting centers in their county. In NYC, each voter is assigned to one early-voting site. Election Day poll sites and early-voting sites should be rechecked before voting because locations can change.

election_day.label: Election Day Voting
election_day.content: New York's General Election is Tuesday, November 3, 2026. Polling places are open from 6:00 a.m. until 9:00 p.m. A voter who is in line by 9:00 p.m. must be allowed to vote. New York generally does not require an already-registered voter to present identification at the polling place. Certain first-time voters whose identity was not verified during registration may be required to provide identification. A voter who has been issued an early mail or absentee ballot may still go to the polls and vote in person; New York election officials will determine which ballot is valid under the state's ballot reconciliation procedures.
election_day.source_name: New York State Board of Elections
election_day.internal_note: The State Board's current homepage directly confirms November 3, 2026 and 6:00 a.m.-9:00 p.m. polling hours. New York does not impose a universal voter-ID requirement. HAVA identification requirements can apply to certain first-time voters who registered by mail and were not previously verified. New York permits a voter who requested or received an early mail or absentee ballot to vote in person; election officials use ballot records to prevent double voting.

polling_hours.label: Polling Hours
polling_hours.content: New York polling places are open from 6:00 a.m. until 9:00 p.m. for the November 3, 2026 General Election. A voter who is in line when the polls close at 9:00 p.m. is entitled to vote.
polling_hours.source_name: New York State Board of Elections
polling_hours.internal_note: The State Board's current 2026 election information directly lists General Election polling hours as 6:00 a.m.-9:00 p.m. New York Election Law Section 8-100 governs polling hours.

early_voting.label: Early In-Person Voting
early_voting.content: New York provides nine days of in-person early voting before Primary, General and Special Elections. For the November 3, 2026 General Election, early voting begins Saturday, October 24 and continues through Sunday, November 1. Hours are established by local County Boards of Elections and vary by county. Outside New York City, voters may use any of their assigned early-voting centers within the county. New York City voters are assigned to a specific early-voting site.
early_voting.source_name: New York State Board of Elections — Early Voting
early_voting.internal_note: The State Board directly confirms nine early-voting days and the October 24-November 1 dates for the 2026 General Election. The official 2026 Political Calendar cites Election Law Section 8-600. Exact hours and locations are county-specific and should be reverified near Election Day.

absentee_mail.label: Early Mail & Absentee Voting
absentee_mail.content: New York provides two principal mail-ballot options. Any registered voter may request an early mail ballot without providing an excuse. Absentee ballots are available to voters who qualify for one of the reasons established by state law, including absence from the county on Election Day, illness or disability, caregiving responsibilities for a person who is ill or physically disabled, or qualifying Veterans Health Administration hospital status. For the November 3, 2026 General Election, mailed and online requests for an early mail or absentee ballot must be received by the County Board of Elections by October 24. In-person applications may be submitted through November 2. A completed ballot returned by mail must be postmarked no later than November 3 and received by the County Board of Elections no later than November 10. A ballot delivered in person to a County Board of Elections or Election Day poll site must be received by 9:00 p.m. on November 3. Ballots may also be delivered to an early-voting site in the voter's county during the October 24 through November 1 early-voting period.
absentee_mail.glance_value: Early mail: no excuse; request by October 24 if mailed or online
absentee_mail.source_name: New York State Board of Elections — Request a Ballot
absentee_mail.internal_note: Important New York distinction: early mail voting is available to any registered voter without an excuse, while absentee voting remains reason-based. The State Board's 2026 deadlines poster directly establishes October 24 for mailed and online requests, November 2 for in-person requests, November 3 as the postmark/in-person return deadline and November 10 as the final receipt date for timely postmarked domestic ballots. Military and overseas ballots have separate deadlines.

voter_id.label: Voter ID Requirements
voter_id.content: New York does not generally require an already-registered voter to show identification at the polling place. Identification may be required for certain first-time voters who registered by mail and whose identity was not verified before Election Day. In those cases, accepted identification can include qualifying photo identification or specified documents showing the voter's name and address. A voter who is subject to the identification requirement but cannot provide acceptable documentation may cast an affidavit ballot under New York's election procedures.
voter_id.source_name: New York State Board of Elections — Frequently Asked Questions
voter_id.internal_note: New York should not be characterized as a universal voter-ID state. The limited identification requirement stems primarily from federal HAVA requirements for certain first-time mail registrants whose identity was not verified during registration. New York uses affidavit ballots when eligibility cannot be established through the ordinary poll-book process.

accessible_voting.label: Accessible Voting
accessible_voting.content: New York provides accessible voting options for voters with disabilities and other access needs. Polling sites are reviewed for accessibility, and voters may request assistance at the polls. Accessible ballot-marking devices are available for in-person voting. Voters with a print disability, including blindness, low vision, dyslexia, dysgraphia, certain learning disabilities and physical disabilities that interfere with using printed materials, may apply for an accessible ballot with electronic accessibility features. Accessible ballots are obtained through the state's Accessible Ballot Application system and must be returned according to New York's ballot-return requirements.
accessible_voting.glance_value: Accessible polling and accessible ballot system available
accessible_voting.source_name: New York State Board of Elections — Accessible Voting
accessible_voting.internal_note: The State Board directly states that any voter requesting assistance is entitled to receive it regardless of the reason. It also operates the Accessible Ballot Application portal for registered voters with print disabilities. The accessible electronic ballot is a ballot-delivery and marking accommodation and should not be described as unrestricted online voting. Accessibility Services & Training can be reached at 518-207-4050 or [accessibility@elections.ny.gov](mailto:accessibility@elections.ny.gov).

military_overseas.label: Military & Overseas Voting
military_overseas.content: New York provides special registration and ballot procedures for eligible military voters, qualifying family members and U.S. citizens living overseas. Covered voters may use the Federal Post Card Application to register and request a ballot and may use New York's electronic ballot-delivery system when eligible. For the November 3, 2026 General Election, October 24 is the deadline for a Board of Elections to receive a mailed ballot application from an eligible military or overseas voter who is not previously registered. For previously registered voters, the mailed application deadline is October 27, and November 2 is the final day to apply in person. A military or overseas ballot must be postmarked no later than November 3 and received by the Board of Elections no later than November 16.
military_overseas.glance_value: FPCA and electronic ballot delivery available
military_overseas.source_name: New York State Board of Elections — Military and Overseas Voting
military_overseas.internal_note: The State Board's current 2026 UOCAVA page directly establishes October 24 for applications from voters not previously registered, October 27 for mailed applications from previously registered voters, November 2 for in-person applications and November 3/November 16 as the postmark and receipt deadlines. New York has been transitioning its military and overseas electronic ballot-delivery platform, so the exact portal should be reverified close to the election.

student_voting.label: College / Student Voting
student_voting.content: College students may register in New York if they meet the state's voter eligibility and residency requirements. A student may establish a New York college residence as a voting residence when it is the student's fixed, permanent and principal home for voting purposes, or may retain another qualifying voting residence. Students should register and vote from only one residence for an election. A student who is registered elsewhere in New York but will be away from that county on Election Day may also use New York's early mail voting option without providing an excuse.
student_voting.glance_value: Students may vote from one qualifying residence
student_voting.source_name: New York State Board of Elections — Register to Vote
student_voting.internal_note: New York voter eligibility is residence-based. New York courts have long recognized that students may establish voting residence at a college address when statutory residency requirements are satisfied. The reader-facing language deliberately avoids implying that merely attending a New York college automatically establishes voting residence. Early mail voting now provides all registered voters a no-excuse mail option, so students do not need to establish absentee eligibility merely because they are away from their home county.

sample_ballot.label: Official Ballot Information
sample_ballot.content: New York voters can use official State and County Board of Elections resources to review election information and ballot contents. Ballot contents depend on the voter's residential address, election district and local contests. For the November 3, 2026 General Election, the State Board's certification of General Election nominations is scheduled for September 9, and County Boards certify nominations and ballot questions on September 10. Voters should review their official local ballot information after certification is complete.
sample_ballot.glance_value: Check State and County Board ballot information after certification
sample_ballot.source_name: New York State Board of Elections — Election Information
sample_ballot.internal_note: The official 2026 Political Calendar sets September 9 for State Board certification of General Election nominations filed with the State Board and September 10 for County Board certification of nominations and questions. New York does not provide one universally applicable statewide sample ballot because local contests vary. Reverify after September certification and before publication of voter-specific ballot information.

contact.label: Contact the State Election Authority
contact.content: New York State Board of Elections, 40 North Pearl Street, Suite 5, Albany, NY 12207-2729. Main phone: 518-474-6220. For voter-specific registration, polling-place, early-voting or ballot questions, contact your County Board of Elections.
contact.source_name: New York State Board of Elections
contact.internal_note: The State Board maintains statewide election oversight while County Boards administer voter registration, polling locations, early voting and ballot processing locally. Accessibility-specific assistance is available at 518-207-4050 and [accessibility@elections.ny.gov](mailto:accessibility@elections.ny.gov). Email addresses are intentionally plain text with no Markdown or mailto wrapper.

official_resources.label: Official State & Local Resources
official_resources.content: Use the New York State Board of Elections website for official statewide election information. The state's voter lookup provides registration status and Election Day and early-voting polling locations. County Boards of Elections administer voter registration records, polling sites, early-voting locations, early mail and absentee ballots and many other voter-specific election functions.
